goal.source_text: Maximize this rocket fin's stability, keep drag low, keep it under 40 g, must fit a 3-inch body tube.

constraints.label: Fins must not overhang the aft end

assumptions: The 40 g limit applies to all fins combined, since no per-fin limit was stated.
The 3-inch body tube (76.2 mm) is the body the fins mount on, so it is not used as a fin dimension limit.
Maximize stability is interpreted as targeting about 2.5 calibers, since a margin above about 3 calibers would weathercock.
Fin count is left free between 3 and 4 because the user did not specify it.
The design velocity of 120 m/s is taken from the input context.
Read '3-inch body tube' as the rocket body: 76.2 mm diameter, fins may not overhang the aft end.

- Trade a small thickness increase against semi_span to move flutter margin off the 1.5 floor, since thickness's flutter gain (2.52 per unit) is larger than its stability cost (-0.14 per unit).
- Keep taper near 0.46 to 0.50 and sweep near 28, since these changed stability and mass only modestly in this generation; the main gains come from span and thickness.

message.summary: run_1201_764a-g05-a01: Flutter margin of 1.512 sits just above the 1.5 constraint floor, so the champion hugs a constraint boundary and small model error could flip feasibility.

run_1201_764a-g05-f07: Aft overhang of 4.649 mm violates the no-overhang rule, and its taper of 0.61 and sweep of 31.5 are outside the champion's neighborhood, so it adds little information about the optimum.
Agent found a feasible 32 g fin, but CMA-ES scored higher on the same budget.
message.body:
Relative to the infeasible seed (60.264 g, aggregate -0.1067), the champion drops from 4 fins to 3, shortens root chord from 90 to 78 mm and semi-span from 60 to 56 mm, and thins the fins from 3.0 to 2.7 mm. Fin mass falls to 32.027 g, under the 40 g cap, and drag falls from 9.783 N to 6.186 N, while stability margin drops from 2.23 to 1.188 cal, well below the 2.5 cal target. The critic describes this as a deliberate trade: span is held near the minimum needed for stability, and thickness buys back flutter margin (1.512, barely above the 1.5 floor). The champion's aggregate of 0.221 is lower than CMA-ES's 0.3845, so the agent did not beat CMA-ES on this budget. CMA-ES's design is feasible, has higher stability (1.934 cal) and flutter margin (1.912), and is 39.664 g, but its drag is 8.495 N, which is higher than the agent's. The agent beat random search, whose best design is infeasible (stability 0.877 cal, aggregate -0.0307). Next, check why the agent's design scored lower despite lower drag and mass, probably the stability-target weighting, and verify flutter margin and stability with a higher-fidelity or physical test before committing to this fin.

**Caveats:** High-fidelity check shows lift slope [?]% lower than the fast model, so real stability margin could be lower than 1.188 cal, which is already near the 1.0 floor.; Flutter margin of 1.512 is only just above the 1.5 floor, and a fast-model error could push it below.; High-fidelity drag is +1.9% (6.303 N vs 6.186 N), so drag ranking against baselines could shift slightly.
